transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Mark Liu (Redwood SE), Sarah Bennett (Montecito Head of Data), Dr. Luis Ortega (CTO), Priya Nair (Compliance), Tom Reyes (ML Eng)

Summary:
Short call to scope a POC focused on data handling requirements: PII identification/redaction, logging/retention settings, and prompt storage concerns for Montecito Health's clinical summarization assistant. Confirm success criteria, workload sizing and benchmark plan, and next steps for security review and pilot timeline.

Topics covered:
- PII and PHI handling (redaction, never store, tokenization)
- Logging and retention configuration (per-route retention TTLs, audit logs)
- Prompt storage: what we persist (prompts, system messages, user identifiers) and opt-outs
- Workload sizing: qps, token distribution, peak concurrency
- Benchmarks: target P95 latency, throughput, and quality gating
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC

Transcript (timestamps ~30-60s increments, imperfect transcription):
00:00 Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we have Mark from solutions eng, and we heard from Sarah earlier about the use case — clinical summarization, right?
00:10 Sarah: yep, thanks aisha. quick note, we want the POC to validate two things: that data never leaves our control in a way that violates HIPAA, and that latency is within our app snappy threshold.
00:20 Dr. Ortega: and also cost predictability — we have to model token costs against our patient triage load.
00:30 Mark: understood, so today we'll zero in on data handling: PII/PHI, logs, retention, prompt storage, and then outline the benchmarks we'll run. does that sound ok?
00:36 Sarah: yes.
00:40 Priya: from compliance perspective we need full audit logs, SSO integration and proof of KMS integration for key material. also, we prefer that any PII be redacted at the edge rather than relying on model-side redaction alone.
00:55 Mark: totally agree. Redwood supports multiple layers: client-side redaction recommended, then agent-level redaction rules, plus redact-on-ingest at the gateway. for the POC we can show both.
01:10 Tom: quick Q — when you say redact-on-ingest, does that mean you don't persist the raw prompt in logs? like, are we able to configure route-level retention to zero?
01:20 Aisha: yes, you can set per-route retention to 0 for hosted logs, or for Dedicated/Private you can disable server-side logging and keep only application-level audit events. we'll share the exact config snippets.
01:35 Mark: there's also the KV-cache concern — if the prompt or context is cached for performance, we can apply hashing or encrypt keys with customer KMS; we also support not caching sensitive routes.
01:50 Priya: hashing is ok but we need to confirm that the hash can't be reversed or linked to patient IDs; HSM-backed keys preferred.
01:58 Mark: yep, HSM/KMS supported — we integrate with common KMS providers and we can show the key rotation and audit trail during the security review.
02:12 Sarah: regarding prompt storage, are system messages and user metadata persisted? we have a rule that patient identifiers must not be stored.
02:22 Mark: system messages are stored by default for diagnostics, but they can be excluded from persistence. we typically store anonymized prompt fingerprints for quality monitoring; for PII heavy routes we can set fingerprint-only mode or zero retention.
02:35 Dr. Ortega: what about embeddings? if we generate embeddings of notes, that's essentially derived PHI, and we need to control retention and indexing.
02:44 Aisha: correct — embeddings can be configured to never be stored, stored encrypted, or rotated out after a short TTL. for the POC we'll propose both: run a bench with embeddings disabled and then one with embeddings encrypted+TTL to measure differences in latency and cost.
02:58 Tom: for workload sizing, here's our rough traffic: 1.2k requests/day, peak 12 rps, average tokens per request around 600 (most are 400-800). concurrency peaks around 8-10 concurrent inference streams.
03:16 Mark: thanks, that'll map to roughly X tokens/sec — quick calc: 12 rps * 600 tokens ~ 7200 tokens/sec at peak, but that's not sustained, so batching strategy matters.
03:28 Sarah: we need P95 latency under 800 ms for short summaries, acceptable up to 1.5s for longer syntheses.
03:35 Mark: on Dedicated hardware we can target p95 ~300-600ms depending on model and quantization; hosted may be slightly higher but more elastic. we'll run benchmarks to give you numbers.
03:45 Priya: what models are you proposing? we prefer an open model we can audit.
03:50 Mark: we can use a Redwood-verified open model family — smaller quantized variant for latency, and a larger variant for quality checks. for POC we'll test both.
03:59 Aisha: success criteria recap: (1) security: demonstrable non-persistence or encrypted storage of PHI; (2) latency: P95 <800ms for short tasks; (3) quality: F1/ROUGE thresholds on our test prompts; (4) cost modeling fits within their projected run rate.
04:18 Dr. Ortega: timeline?
04:20 Aisha: we typically do a 2-3 week POC: week 1 setup and redaction rules + kickoff, week 2 run benchmarks and iterate, week 3 validate results and handoff. because you have compliance gating, add a parallel security review which can take a week. so total 3-4 weeks from kickoff.
04:40 Priya: we'll need to run an internal legal review; can Redwood supply a SOC2 + architecture diagram?
04:46 Aisha: yes, we'll send SOC2, TrueNorth audit summary, the KMS/HSM integration doc, and the architectural diagram showing data flow.
04:55 Tom: for the benchmark inputs, is there a safe way to send representative traffic? we can't send real PHI.
05:02 Mark: we recommend local client-side redaction to strip direct identifiers, then provide a synthetic but distribution-preserving dataset. alternatively we can run a remote enclave-style benchmark where you run tests in your VPC and we provide the benchmark tooling.
05:16 Sarah: the enclave option sounds appealing — what's the easiest path?
05:20 Mark: for Dedicated inside your VPC or with Private deployment we can run the benchmark in your environment; that removes egress concerns. for hosted we do redacted data. both are standard.
05:31 Priya: logging retention — we need to keep full audit logs for 6 years per our policy but request that prompts be redacted; is that feasible?
05:40 Aisha: yes, audit events and metadata (who called what route and timestamps) can be retained for compliance, while payloads can be redacted or set to short TTL. we'll include sample retention policies you can pick.
05:52 Mark: also to note, debugging can be harder with full redaction — we typically recommend keeping a hashed fingerprint and a minimal anonymized context to repro P0 regressions. we'll show how to map fingerprints back during a joint incident triage without exposing PHI.
06:10 Dr. Ortega: ok that tradeoff is understood.
06:14 Tom: question about prompt-history: we have long context windows and sometimes store user conversation history for context. can we selectively persist only non-PII fields?
06:25 Mark: yes — you can configure which keys are persisted. e.g., store note_text anonymized, store metadata like patient_age bucketed, and drop patient_name/ssn fields. we can provide the ingestion schema and example transforms.
06:39 Sarah: and what about webhook logs and third-party integrations? we have downstream services that receive output, we need assurance those outputs don't carry PHI if we don't want them to.
06:50 Aisha: Redwood can mask or redact outputs sent to webhooks, or you can configure a filter step to scrub outputs server-side before pushing. for Private deployments, outputs never leave your VPC unless you configure them to.
07:05 Priya: regarding encryption, we need proof of envelope encryption and key rotation policies.
07:12 Mark: we use envelope encryption with customer-managed keys; rotation and usage logs appear in audit trails. we'll include a sample key rotation schedule and logs in the security pack.
07:24 Sarah: benchmark specifics — what do you propose we measure?
07:27 Mark: baseline plan: run 10k representative queries (redacted) across short summary and long synth tasks, measure P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput (reqs/sec), token cost per response, and quality metrics (ROUGE/LU) against your gold set. run with two model configs: quantized low-latency and standard quality mode.
07:45 Tom: can you also test with embeddings off vs on?
07:48 Mark: yes, embeddings-on + encrypted storage vs embeddings-off to show cost/latency delta.
07:53 Aisha: timeline-wise we'll need your redaction rules and sample dataset by Dec 22 to hit benchmark execution by Dec 23. results shared by Dec 24 and then a follow-up deep-dive week of Dec 29.
08:06 Priya: can Redwood redact dynamically at inference time using rules? like scrub PHI patterns?
08:15 Mark: we have regex & ML-driven PII detectors that can operate client-side or server-side; we strongly recommend client-side as first line but server-side is available as fallback. detectors are configurable per-route.
08:28 Sarah: ok, last thing on cost: we want to model monthly run rate; who provides the cost model?
08:33 Aisha: we'll provide a cost spreadsheet: tokens billed, embeddings billed, storage billed, and run a couple of scenario projections based on your traffic numbers.
08:42 Dr. Ortega: any blockers?
08:44 Priya: none besides legal signoff and redaction rules.
08:47 Tom: i'll prepare the sample traffic (synthetic) and the list of PII fields.
08:52 Aisha: perfect. i'll send SOC2 and security pack, Mark will run the benchmark, we'll schedule the deep-dive.
08:58 Sarah: thanks all.
09:02 Aisha: recap of next steps: send docs, run bench, schedule deep-dive. we'll follow up on slack/email. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
